g: (biochemistry) A protein found on the surface of certain immune and blood cells that binds to antibodies attached to infected cells or invading pathogens, enabling antibody-mediated phagocytosis or antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC).

(immunology, biochemistry, molecular biology) The portion of an antibody formed from the constant region domains of the heavy chain that constitutes the tail and mediates effector functions such as complement activation and Fc receptor binding.
